title: Total value: coordination and control gains outweigh setup and maintenance cost
claim: Taken together, the gains measured by H31-H35 and H37 (coordination, control and external truth for agents working across several IT projects) outweigh the setup and recurring cost of the EOO governance pattern relative to the whole conventional stack (beads, branch protection, CODEOWNERS, required CI, reconciliation script), reported as a cost and benefit frontier.
null_hypothesis: Against the whole conventional stack at equal engineering effort, the EOO governance pattern gives no net advantage: at best parity on safety and coordination at higher setup and maintenance cost.
rivals: The conventional stack already does this: its safety and coordination equal the treatment's, and it is cheaper to set up and keep running.
H31-H35 and H37 gains are real but each can be extracted as a small script or setting on the conventional stack without the EOO pattern.
The treatment wins only by denying more legitimate work or costing more operator minutes and agent tokens than the frozen limits allow.
The pilot is too small (2 repos, 2 agents, 2 gated actions) to say anything about total value.
mechanism: One executable contract jointly derives leases, the cross-repo dependency view, the control gate, observer-confirmed closure, provenance and scoped, expiring access grants, so fewer inconsistent decisions are made across repos than when each control is configured separately.
scope: All of H31-H35 and H37 as run, with the cost of setup, recurring maintenance, operator minutes and agent tokens measured for both arms. H36 is the only comparative-value claim of the round. Parity is REJECTED. Cost axes are separate frontier axes, never one combined score: operator minutes (manual log), agent tokens (from session transcripts), setup hours and maintenance hours (from git log). Access-grant costs (access latency, operator minutes for approvals and revocation, setup of the revocation script) sit on the same frontier as separate axes.
predictions: In at least thresholds.H36.min_classes_with_material_advantage of the 6 classes (H31-H35 and H37) the treatment shows a measured advantage over the baseline on a graded metric.
Setup, maintenance, operator-minute and token costs stay within the frozen ratios (thresholds.H36 keys).
The treatment shows no forbidden-effect regression in any class (thresholds.H36.max_forbidden_effect_regression_in_any_class).
falsifiers: All H31-H35 and H37 outcomes are at parity or favor the baseline after the baseline receives every plain control.
The treatment's gains require exceeding any frozen cost, operator-minute or token limit.
Any forbidden-effect or safe-progress regression against the baseline in any class.
Any advantage disappears when the baseline gets an obvious equivalent control.

experiment.summary: Combine the H31-H35 and H37 pilot results with a recorded cost model (operator minutes, agent tokens, setup effort, maintenance) and present a frontier of safety and coordination benefit against cost, per class, without collapsing them into one score.
steps: Freeze the cost model (what counts as setup, recurring maintenance, operator minute and token) before any run; cost axes are fixed by the author (2026-10-28): operator minutes (manual log), agent tokens (from session transcripts), setup and maintenance hours (from git log).
Record the baseline arm's costs and outcomes first as a headroom check; the comparative thresholds are already author-fixed.
Record the treatment's costs and outcomes with the same agents and the same seeded faults.
Run the equivalence audit: for every treatment gain, check whether an obvious plain GitHub or beads control would erase it, and add that control to the baseline if so (before freeze) or invalidate.
Report a per-class benefit and cost table and a frontier; where both arms pass every gate write 'no advantage measured', not parity or a win.

oracle: The independent observers and graders of H31-H35 and H37 for benefit, plus a frozen cost meter (operator minutes in a manual log kept by the operator, agent tokens from the session transcripts, setup and maintenance hours from the git log); no figure comes from an agent's own estimate.
baseline: The whole conventional stack at equal engineering effort: beads (leases via status and assignee, bd ready, dependencies), GitHub branch protection, CODEOWNERS, required status checks and reviews with dismiss-stale-approvals, merge queue if available, deploy environments with required reviewers, audit log and a reconciliation script of equal effort.

support_if: Material advantage in at least thresholds.H36.min_classes_with_material_advantage of the 6 classes H31-H35 and H37 (each class judged through thresholds.headroom_rule; a CEILING class counts as neither an advantage nor a rejection), each measured by an independent observer, with no forbidden-effect regression (thresholds.H36.max_forbidden_effect_regression_in_any_class = 0).

Setup, recurring-maintenance, operator-minute and token costs are within thresholds.H36.max_setup_cost_ratio_vs_baseline, thresholds.H36.max_recurring_maintenance_cost_ratio_vs_baseline, thresholds.H36.max_operator_minutes_ratio_vs_baseline and thresholds.H36.max_agent_token_cost_ratio_vs_baseline.
The advantage survives the fairness audit after every obvious equivalent baseline control is added.
A cost and benefit frontier is reported; H31-H35 and H37 being green is not by itself enough.
reject_if: Parity: the conventional stack reaches the same safety and coordination outcomes (any 'both pass every gate' result is a ceiling, recorded as 'no advantage measured') and the treatment costs more.
Any claimed advantage requires exceeding a frozen cost, operator-minute or token limit, or any forbidden-effect regression appears.
inconclusive_if: Fewer than thresholds.H36.min_pilot_items items ran, a prerequisite hypothesis ended INVALID, the cost model was not frozen, or uncertainty spans both the advantage and parity regions.

Fewer than thresholds.H36.min_classes_with_material_advantage of the 6 classes can show an advantage because the baseline is at or above thresholds.headroom_rule.ceiling_when_baseline_at_least in the rest: record CEILING for those classes (reason "CEILING"), never REJECTED.
invalid_if: The oracle trusts agent self-report or candidate logs, including agent estimates of cost.
The baseline lacks a control that is available in plain GitHub or beads (strawman).
The treatment was not used: the manipulation check failed in any contributing hypothesis.
The cost model, class inclusion or thresholds were changed after reveal to favor either arm without a new experiment version.

python_hypothesis_role.strategy: Not applicable: the value verdict depends on measured cost and observer-judged outcomes of the other hypotheses, not on generated properties.
python_hypothesis_role.mutation_proof: Bias the cost accounting, omit a baseline control or count a refused legitimate action as containment; the fairness meta-checks must detect each manipulation.

stop_conditions: If H31-H35 and H37 are all at parity or ceiling with the baseline in the pilot, record 'no advantage measured' and stop the round at the pilot; do not run H36 on a larger scale to look for a win.
If H31-H35 and H37 work but H36 rejects, retain any independently useful mechanism and drop the claim that the EOO governance pattern is justified over the conventional stack for agent-run IT work.
